question: As of April 2022, what is the FDI limit in the insurance sector in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**up to 74%**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• As of April 2022, the FDI limit in the** insurance sector in India is up to 74%.**
 
• The** Foreign Direct Investment (FDI**) limit in the insurance sector was raised from **49% to 74%** in March 2021 through amendments to the **Insurance Act, 1938**.
 
• This change was made to attract foreign capital, boost the insurance penetration in the country, and improve financial inclusion.
 
• By April 2022, t**his policy was fully implemented.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Impact of the Change**:

 
• **Enhanced Capital Availability**: Increased FDI brought in much-needed capital, enabling insurance companies to expand operations and enhance their reach.
 
• **Boosting Insurance Penetration**: India's insurance penetration was relatively low, at around 4.2% of GDP (in terms of premiums) in FY21, compared to the global average. The increase in FDI aimed to address this gap.
 
• **Encouraging Competition**: It encouraged global players to invest in Indian insurers, leading to more competition and improved products and services.
